q: Statement: Many students in a college hostel fell ill after eating food from the hostel mess. Courses of action: I. The college should have the mess kitchen and its stored food inspected for hygiene. II. The college should close the hostel permanently. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Inspecting the kitchen deals directly with the likely cause of the illness. Closing the hostel for good is an extreme step that punishes all residents.

q: Statement: During the dengue season, a city hospital reports a sharp rise in dengue patients from one neighbourhood. Courses of action: I. The health department should spray the neighbourhood and remove standing water where mosquitoes breed. II. Residents of the neighbourhood should be advised to cover water containers and use mosquito repellent. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Both steps are practical and act directly on mosquito breeding and bites in the affected area, so both follow.

q: Statement: A busy junction in Rawalpindi gets jammed every afternoon at school closing time because parents park their cars on the road. Courses of action: I. The school should be shifted to another city. II. Traffic police should be posted at the junction at school closing time to stop roadside parking. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Posting traffic police at the peak time tackles the stated cause, roadside parking. Moving the school to another city is impractical and extreme.

q: Statement: Many candidates reached an entry-test centre late because the centre's address printed on the admit card was unclear. Courses of action: I. Future admit cards should print the full address of the centre along with a nearby landmark. II. All candidates who arrived on time should be made to sit the test again. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: A clearer address fixes the stated cause of lateness. Retesting the candidates who were on time does nothing about the unclear address.

q: Statement: Smog levels in Lahore rise sharply every November, and hospitals see more patients with breathing problems. Courses of action: I. All vehicles in Lahore should be banned for the whole winter. II. People with asthma and other breathing problems should be advised to limit time outdoors on high-smog days. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Advising at-risk people to limit exposure is practical and protects them directly. A total vehicle ban for a whole season is extreme and unworkable.

q: Statement: A government hospital's emergency ward has long waits because patients with minor complaints and seriously ill patients stand in the same queue. Courses of action: I. A triage desk should be set up to sort patients by how urgently they need care. II. Patients with minor complaints should be refused treatment at the hospital. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Triage directly solves the mixed-queue problem. Refusing treatment to a whole group of patients is extreme and not acceptable.

q: Statement: A college library is overcrowded during exam weeks, and many students cannot find a seat. Courses of action: I. The library should stay open for longer hours during exam weeks. II. Spare classrooms should be opened as study rooms during exam weeks. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Longer hours spread users over more time and spare rooms add seats. Both are practical and address the shortage of seats, so both follow.

q: Statement: A survey finds that many pupils in a town skip breakfast and feel tired and unable to concentrate in morning classes. Courses of action: I. Morning classes should be cancelled in all schools of the town. II. Schools should hold awareness sessions for pupils and parents on the importance of breakfast. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Awareness sessions act on the cause, skipping breakfast. Cancelling all morning classes is extreme and does not solve the problem.

q: Statement: Tests show that the tap water in one residential area contains sewage because of a leaking pipe. Courses of action: I. The water authority should repair the leaking pipe without delay. II. Residents should be advised to boil their drinking water until the repair is complete. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Repairing the pipe removes the cause, and boiling water protects residents meanwhile. Both are practical and direct, so both follow.

q: Statement: A drug inspector found a medical store in a city selling medicines after their expiry date. Courses of action: I. All medical stores in the city should be closed. II. Action should be taken against that store under the drug laws. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Acting against the store that broke the rule is direct and lawful. Closing every store in the city because of one store is extreme.

q: Statement: Many first-year students at a medical college say they cannot follow lectures because they are delivered too quickly. Courses of action: I. Teachers should be asked to slow their pace and share lecture notes with students. II. The college should increase its tuition fee. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: A slower pace and shared notes address the stated difficulty. Raising the fee has nothing to do with the problem.

q: Statement: A new flyover opened in a city last month, but traffic jams have now shifted to the next signal, where flyover traffic meets a narrow road. Courses of action: I. The flyover should be demolished. II. Traffic engineers should study that signal and adjust its timing and the road layout there. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: The stated problem is the bottleneck at the next signal, which a traffic study and retiming address. Demolishing the flyover is extreme and wastes what already works.

q: Statement: In a village, many children missed their polio drops because their families were away when the vaccination team visited. Courses of action: I. The vaccination team should make a follow-up visit to cover the children who were missed. II. The families who were away should be fined. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: A follow-up visit reaches the missed children directly. Fining families for being away is punitive and does not get the children vaccinated.

q: Statement: During a class test, a few students were found using mobile phones. Courses of action: I. Mobile phones should be banned throughout the country. II. Every student in the class should be failed in the test. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: A nationwide ban is far beyond the problem, and failing the whole class punishes students who did nothing wrong. Both are extreme, so neither follows.

q: Statement: During a heatwave in Sindh, several labourers working outdoors at midday suffered heatstroke. Courses of action: I. Employers should be advised to move outdoor work to cooler hours and provide drinking water and shade. II. Hospitals in the area should be prepared to treat heatstroke cases. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: The first step prevents further heatstroke and the second ensures those affected get prompt care. Both are practical responses to the stated problem.

q: Statement: Many passengers at a railway station complain that they cannot hear the announcements about platform changes. Courses of action: I. The station should stop announcing platform changes. II. The station's loudspeakers should be checked, and display boards showing platform changes should be installed. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Better speakers and display boards make the information reach passengers. Stopping announcements makes the problem worse.

q: Statement: A road in a town has many potholes, and several motorcyclists have had accidents there after rain. Courses of action: I. The road should be repaired. II. Motorcycles should be banned in the town. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Repairing the potholes removes the cause of the accidents. Banning all motorcycles is extreme.

q: Statement: Each year many students fail the chemistry practical exam because their college laboratory has too few working instruments. Courses of action: I. The chemistry practical should be removed from the course. II. The college should repair its broken instruments and buy more. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Fixing and adding instruments deals with the shortage that causes failure. Removing the practical avoids the problem instead of solving it.

q: Statement: One bus of a private transport company broke down on the motorway, delaying its passengers for two hours. Courses of action: I. The company's licence should be cancelled at once. II. All private buses should be banned from the motorway. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: A single breakdown does not justify cancelling a licence, and banning every private bus punishes companies that did nothing wrong. Both are extreme.

q: Statement: Cases of diarrhoea among children in a district rise every summer, and many are linked to unsafe drinking water. Courses of action: I. Health workers should teach families how to keep drinking water safe and how to use ORS. II. The district's water supply should be tested regularly. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Teaching families protects children directly, and testing the supply finds unsafe water. Both are practical and aimed at the stated cause.

q: Statement: Sara scored low marks in an MDCAT mock test because she ran out of time in the last section. Courses of action: I. She should practise timed tests to improve her speed. II. She should give up her plan to study medicine. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Timed practice deals directly with running out of time. Giving up her goal over one mock test is extreme.

q: Statement: A newly built hospital in a town has a modern CT scanner, but no trained staff to operate it. Courses of action: I. The CT scanner should be sold. II. Staff should be trained or hired to operate the CT scanner. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: The problem is the lack of trained staff, which training or hiring solves. Selling the scanner throws away a useful machine.

q: Statement: Long queues form at a university's fee counter on the last date of fee payment every semester. Courses of action: I. The university should let students pay fees online or through banks. II. The last date should be announced well in advance and reminders sent, so that payments are spread out. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Online or bank payment reduces counter traffic, and early notice spreads payments over more days. Both are practical and direct.

q: Statement: A school cricket match had to be stopped halfway when it started to rain. Courses of action: I. Cricket should be banned at the school. II. The school should build a roof over its cricket ground. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Rain stopping one match is not a problem that needs action. Banning cricket is extreme and roofing a whole ground is impractical, so neither follows.

q: Statement: Many patients at a district hospital stop taking their antibiotics early, and their infections come back. Courses of action: I. Doctors and pharmacists should explain to patients why the full course must be completed. II. The hospital should stop prescribing antibiotics. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Explaining the full course tackles the stated cause. Stopping antibiotics altogether would leave infections untreated.

q: Statement: Many pedestrians are injured while crossing a busy road outside a market because there is no safe crossing. Courses of action: I. The market should be closed. II. A signal-controlled zebra crossing or a pedestrian bridge should be built near the market. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: A safe crossing deals directly with the stated cause of the injuries. Closing the market is extreme and harms traders and shoppers.

q: Statement: An electricity company finds that power is being stolen through illegal connections in some areas, overloading transformers and causing breakdowns. Courses of action: I. The company should find and remove the illegal connections and act against those responsible under the law. II. Electricity to the whole city should be cut off until the theft stops. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Removing illegal connections addresses the cause directly and lawfully. Cutting power to the whole city punishes everyone and is extreme.

q: Statement: Students of a college complain that the college bus often leaves before their evening classes end. Courses of action: I. The bus timetable should be changed to match the end of evening classes. II. Students should be told to arrange their own transport. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Matching the bus timing to class times solves the problem. Telling students to manage on their own ignores the problem rather than solving it.

q: Statement: After heavy monsoon rain, many streets in Karachi were flooded because the drains were blocked with garbage. Courses of action: I. The city's drains should be cleaned before the next monsoon. II. Citizens should be made aware not to throw garbage into drains. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Cleaning removes the present blockage, and awareness prevents new blockages. Both deal with the stated cause, so both follow.

q: Statement: A teacher noticed that a few students in her class had copied their homework from one another. Courses of action: I. Homework should be abolished in the school. II. The students involved should be expelled from the school. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Abolishing homework for everyone and expelling students over copied homework are both far too extreme for the problem, so neither follows.

q: Statement: A survey shows that many young people in a city do not know the warning signs of diabetes. Courses of action: I. Awareness campaigns about the warning signs of diabetes should be run in colleges and on the media. II. A law should require every young person in the city to have a blood test every month. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Awareness campaigns fill the stated knowledge gap. A monthly compulsory blood test for everyone is impractical and extreme.

q: Statement: An examination board found that the question paper of one subject had reached some candidates before the exam. Courses of action: I. The exam in that subject should be held again with a new paper. II. The board should investigate how the paper leaked and tighten the security of question papers. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: A fresh exam restores fairness for this paper, and the inquiry prevents future leaks. Both are practical and directly address the leak.

q: Statement: Many children in a town fall ill after eating cut fruit sold uncovered by street vendors. Courses of action: I. Vendors should be required to keep cut fruit covered and clean. II. Food inspectors should check street vendors regularly. III. All street vending in the town should be banned. Which course(s) of action follow?
o: I, II and III all follow
x: Covering food and regular inspection both deal with unhygienic selling. A total ban on street vending is extreme, so only I and II follow.

q: Statement: A medical college finds that many of its students suffer from stress and anxiety before their professional exams. Courses of action: I. The college should give students access to a trained counsellor. II. Professional exams should be cancelled. III. Teachers should guide students on study planning and time management. Which course(s) of action follow?
o: I, II and III all follow
x: Counselling and study guidance both help students cope with exam stress. Cancelling professional exams is extreme and impractical, so only I and III follow.

q: Statement: Many motorcyclists in a city suffer head injuries in accidents because they do not wear helmets. Courses of action: I. Traffic police should enforce the law that requires helmets. II. Motorcycles should be banned in the city. III. Campaigns should be run to make riders aware of the need to wear helmets. Which course(s) of action follow?
o: I, II and III all follow
x: Enforcing the helmet law and awareness campaigns both increase helmet use. Banning motorcycles is extreme, so only I and III follow.

q: Statement: Patients at a hospital sometimes receive the wrong medicine because doctors' handwritten prescriptions are hard to read. Courses of action: I. Prescriptions should be typed or printed. II. Pharmacists should confirm any unclear prescription with the doctor before giving the medicine. III. Doctors whose handwriting is unclear should be dismissed. Which course(s) of action follow?
o: I, II and III all follow
x: Printed prescriptions remove the cause, and checking with the doctor catches errors. Dismissing doctors for their handwriting is extreme, so only I and II follow.

q: Statement: Many students in a college fail their English paper because they cannot write a proper essay in the time allowed. Courses of action: I. The English paper should be removed from the course. II. The college should hold extra classes for timed essay-writing practice. III. Students who fail English should be expelled. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Timed essay practice tackles the stated weakness. Removing the paper avoids the problem and expulsion is extreme, so only II follows.

q: Statement: A district hospital's blood bank is short of blood, and patients who need surgery are waiting. Courses of action: I. Blood donation camps should be organised in colleges and offices. II. The blood bank should call its registered donors to come and donate. III. The hospital should arrange blood from nearby blood banks for urgent cases. Which course(s) of action follow?
o: I, II and III all follow
x: All three are practical: camps and registered donors refill the stock, while nearby blood banks cover urgent cases now. So all three follow.

q: Statement: Drivers on a long highway often fall asleep at the wheel at night and cause accidents. Courses of action: I. Rest areas should be built along the highway, and drivers should be advised to take regular breaks. II. Night travel on all highways should be banned. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Rest areas and breaks deal directly with driver tiredness. A ban on all night travel is extreme and impractical.

q: Statement: A college's records show that students who attend fewer than half of their classes usually fail their exams. Courses of action: I. The college should monitor attendance and inform the parents of students whose attendance is low. II. Students with low attendance should be given extra marks so that they pass. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Monitoring attendance and involving parents addresses the cause. Giving free marks hides the problem and is unfair to others.

q: Statement: A power fault stopped a city's traffic signals during rush hour, causing jams at many junctions. Courses of action: I. All cars should be banned from the city centre. II. Traffic police should control the junctions by hand until the signals are repaired. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Manual control by traffic police is the practical temporary fix for broken signals. Banning all cars from the centre is extreme.

q: Statement: A newspaper reported that one fast-food outlet in a city had served stale meat to its customers. Courses of action: I. All fast-food outlets in the country should be closed. II. People should be advised to stop eating meat altogether. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: The problem is one outlet, so closing every outlet in the country and giving up meat are both extreme. Neither follows; acting against that outlet would.

q: Statement: Many candidates fill in their entry-test application forms incorrectly, and their applications are rejected. Courses of action: I. Clear instructions and a sample filled-in form should be published with the application. II. A help desk and telephone helpline should be set up to answer applicants' questions. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Clear instructions prevent mistakes, and a helpline lets applicants clear their doubts. Both directly reduce errors in the forms.

q: Statement: The only lift in a five-storey hospital has broken down, and patients in wheelchairs cannot reach the upper floors. Courses of action: I. The lift should be repaired at once. II. The upper floors of the hospital should be demolished. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Repairing the lift solves the problem directly. Demolishing floors is absurdly extreme.

q: Statement: A university finds that most of its students know very little about first aid. Courses of action: I. The university should stop all sports so that no one gets hurt. II. The university should offer first-aid training workshops to its students. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Workshops fill the stated gap in first-aid knowledge. Stopping all sports does not teach first aid and is extreme.

q: Statement: A school notices that many of its pupils have weak eyesight but have never had their eyes tested. Courses of action: I. The school should arrange free eye tests for its pupils. II. Parents of pupils found to have weak eyesight should be advised to see an eye specialist. III. Pupils with weak eyesight should be moved to a separate school. Which course(s) of action follow?
o: I, II and III all follow
x: Eye tests find the problem and referral to a specialist treats it. Moving pupils to another school is extreme and does not help their eyes, so only I and II follow.

q: Statement: Ambulances in a city are often delayed in traffic because other drivers do not give way to them. Courses of action: I. Drivers should be made aware of the need to give way to ambulances, and the rule should be enforced. II. Ambulances should not operate during rush hour. Which course(s) of action follow?
x: Awareness and enforcement make drivers give way, which solves the delay. Stopping ambulances at rush hour would leave patients without help.
